guarantees.claim: cmd_q always equals the type-cast value of reg2hw.cmd.cmd.q as kmac_cmd_e.
sw_cmd equals cmd_q when cmd_update is true, otherwise CmdNone.

assumptions.claim: reg2hw.cmd.cmd.q is always a legal encoding of kmac_cmd_e.
assumptions.risk: If reg2hw.cmd.cmd.q holds an illegal encoding, cmd_q may be an undefined enum value and sw_cmd can propagate an invalid command to downstream logic, potentially causing undefined behavior.

assumptions.claim: Software asserts reg2hw.cmd.cmd.qe for exactly one cycle per command, with reg2hw.cmd.cmd.q holding the intended command value stable during that cycle.
assumptions.risk: If qe toggles incorrectly or q changes while qe is asserted, sw_cmd may capture an incorrect or unstable command, leading to wrong operation.

uncertain_points.claim: No validation is performed on reg2hw.cmd.cmd.q to ensure it corresponds to a legal kmac_cmd_e enumeration. An invalid value could be passed directly to sw_cmd.
uncertain_points.cond: when reg2hw.cmd.cmd.q is an illegal enum value
uncertain_points.risk: Downstream command decoding may misinterpret the illegal value, potentially leading to unintended operations or security violations.

uncertain_points.claim: sw_cmd is combinational and could glitch if cmd_update or cmd_q have timing glitches, possibly triggering spurious commands before they stabilize.
uncertain_points.cond: if cmd_update toggles due to register write timing or if cmd_q changes near a clock edge
uncertain_points.risk: A spurious command might be latched by downstream logic, causing unintended operations and potential security state corruption.
